answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms cannot hit the target this cycle; defer_decision risks a coverage gap since the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renewal. memory_c2 is the load-bearing evidence for switching (sharp unit-cost cut, quick onboarding, accurate invoicing), so I want it verified before committing — it is the one memory whose failure mode would be catastrophic at 94% line utilization with zero buffer. memory_c3 supports qualifying the alternate as a hedge, and memory_c1 warns that switching sacrifices integration stability, which is why I frame this as a guarded initial transition (partial volume to the low-cost vendor, incumbent retained as bridge/secondary through expiry) rather than a broad rollover. If verification of c2 undermines the onboarding or invoicing claims, I fall back to add_second_source this cycle and pursue the switch next review.
